title: Main-frame response streamed through shouldInterceptRequest renders progressively (gate=beacon)

results.condition: Progressive in WebView read blocks only: the first read takes the bytes that InputStream.available() reports, then the WebView fills each 2048-byte read before it passes bytes to the renderer, so a smaller flush waits for more bytes or the end of the body (block-1500 runs: 4 s stall)

Progressive in 64 KiB blocks only: each native read asks for the free space of a 64 KiB Mojo data pipe and the stream read fills it, so a page or a flush smaller than the block reaches the renderer only with the next bytes or at the end of the body (small-2048 runs: all 7 gates timed out, beacons only after the last chunk); WebView 91 has no DOCUMENT_START_SCRIPT, so page scripts that run before the load ends cannot reach a document-start bridge

title: Native early fetch started before the WebView exists is reused as the intercepted main-frame response
Status and fields (including Content-Security-Policy) of the intercepted response reach the page; the reason phrase is not observable from the page
Redirect of the main document when the native fetch meets a 3xx

results.condition: A redirected document is never streamed: the early fetch does not follow a 3xx (CL-44), the rule passes the request (no byte delivered, so no cache result and no public partition, H-67), and the WebView requests the first URL again and follows the redirect itself (one extra request); a 3xx WebResourceResponse is refused by its constructor (status 300-399), and shouldInterceptRequest is not called for the redirect targets (shouldOverrideUrlLoading is, with isRedirect)

title: Partial response: Range request and 206 for a subresource; a cut main-frame stream ends in a normal load

results.condition: A main-frame stream that ends with an error before the document committed gives an error page (net::ERR_FAILED), not the delivered bytes; after the commit (partial set: /s/cut hold) the WebView calls onPageStarted, onReceivedError (net::ERR_FAILED) and onPageFinished but keeps the partial page (readyState loading, the delivered text, no error page). In both cases the session must detect the error and call loadUrl again (CL-33). Range requests of subresources pass unchanged: the interceptor sees the Range field, the page gets 206 with the right bytes and 416 for a bad range

title: IOS-P1: early URLSession fetch and loadSimulatedRequest(_:response:responseData:) render the page; first render time
IOS-P1: document.location, window.origin and relative URLs after loadSimulatedRequest and after loadHTMLString with a base URL
IOS-P1: cookies (document.cookie, HttpOnly cookie sent on a same-origin fetch) after loadSimulatedRequest

results.condition: WebKit ignores the Set-Cookie field of the simulated response and does not share the native URLSession cookies; the SDK must put the cookies of its native fetch into the WKHTTPCookieStore of the web view (setCookie, wait for the completion) before loadSimulatedRequest. With this sync (CAP-I-11) the page has the native cookies with their attributes: document.cookie shows all but the HttpOnly one, and same-origin fetches send all. Cookies that the page sets (HttpOnly by fetch, script cookies) work and go with same-origin fetches.

results.condition: navigator.serviceWorker is missing in a normal app with every prototype (loadSimulatedRequest, loadHTMLString, load(URLRequest), rqlab). Only in an app that declares WKAppBoundDomains in its Info.plist and sets limitsNavigationsToAppBoundDomains (lab build AppBound, runs <os>/app-bound/) does an https page of an app-bound domain register a worker, and the worker controls the page after one reload (a real WebKit navigation, so with IOS-P1 not the snapshot); a rqlab page gets TypeError. title: History, back and forward, and the navigation delegate per prototype

results.condition: load(URLRequest) and rqlab pages have normal history: link clicks add entries, goBack/goForward and history.go work, decidePolicyFor gives link and back_forward. IOS-P1 differs: the loadSimulatedRequest entry is in the back-forward list, but back to it loads the URL again from the network (the given data is not reused, so the SDK must handle a back_forward navigation to that entry itself if it wants its snapshot); loadHTMLString makes no entry of its own (the first navigation replaces it). no-store https pages are fetched again on back and forward; rqlab pages come from the page cache without a handler call. App loads and script navigations both have the type other.

title: Cookie sync between WKHTTPCookieStore and HTTPCookieStorage for HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite

results.condition: Sync works in both directions and keeps HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite=Strict/Lax (native HTTPCookieStorage -> WKHTTPCookieStore.setCookie before the load; getAllCookies -> HTTPCookieStorage before a native fetch); WebKit then hides HttpOnly from document.cookie and does not send a SameSite=Strict cookie on a top-level navigation that a cross-site page starts. Conditions: URLSession does not apply SameSite (a native fetch sends Strict and Lax cookies also with a cross-site mainDocumentURL), so the SDK may use its native fetch only when the web view is blank or shows a page of the same site as the target, where WebKit also sends them (set initiator: on 26.5 and 27.0 WebKit withholds Strict also on an app-started load of another site; 18.5 sends it); cross-site subresources and iframes of the web view get no cookies at all (WebKit third-party cookie blocking), whatever the sync; SameSite=None and no SameSite are not told apart by HTTPCookie.sameSitePolicy (the value differs by iOS version), so the SDK must not depend on that value.

title: URL serialization of OkHttp HttpUrl, java.net.URI, android.net.Uri, Foundation URL and URLComponents against WHATWG

results.condition: No native URL type equals WHATWG for all inputs (67 URLs): OkHttp HttpUrl matches WHATWG on every Q-24 query class (57/67 equal; differs on `|` in the path, a space in the fragment, numeric IPv4 forms, the host `.` and port 0); java.net.URI 19/67 (refuses 19 inputs WHATWG accepts); Foundation URL and URLComponents 28/67 on macOS and on the iOS 27.0 simulator, and they read `https://a.example\@b.example/p` with host b.example (WHATWG: a.example); android.net.Uri 22/67 (returns the input as written, no resolve API). So the SDK serializes the URL of the binding with OkHttp on Android and must not take a host or a serialization from Foundation on iOS (DL-040); closure of Q-24 stays with WP-13 (DL-135)
